rounds.proof_sketch: Kernel launch uses dim3 threads(threads_count) which sets threadIdx.x to range [0, out_features-1] while threadIdx.y = 0 always. Mutation changes out_idx from threadIdx.x to threadIdx.y, making out_idx = 0 for ALL threads. However, the kernel's output is hardcoded: output[batch_idx] = 1.0f (line 68 in original, line 68 in mutant). Regardless of mutation's effect on intermediate computations (matmul, dropout, shared memory), the observable output is always a constant 1.0 tensor.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the thread indexing such that all threads see out_idx = 0 instead of their unique thread index. This causes all threads to compute the same weight column (column 0), write to the same shared memory location (race condition at shared_sum[0]), and all threads enter the reduction block (since all have out_idx == 0). However, the final output line is hardcoded as output[batch_idx] = 1.0f — this value does not depend on any computation result (mean_val is computed but never used). Since both original and mutant write 1.0f to every output position, they are observationally equivalent regardless of input values.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under current contract. The output is a compile-time constant (1.0f) that does not depend on any input or intermediate computation. The softmax-over-single-element optimization hardcodes the result, making the mutation's internal effects invisible at the output level. No value-level test can distinguish them because no value affects the output.
rounds.recommendations: This mutation survives because the kernel contains dead computation — the matmul, dropout, and mean results are computed but discarded since softmax(single_element) = 1.0 is hardcoded. To create killable mutations, either: (1) modify the kernel to actually use the mean value before softmax, (2) test intermediate values via output tensor augmentation, or (3) restructure the operation to avoid the constant-output optimization when testing individual kernel components.
